design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (independent_living_billing_and_move_out) - Whitcombe household, Larkspur at Willow Creek.

[Step 0 - draw and scope] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"task": 0, "key": "env_0034_senior_living_operator/independent_living_billing_and_move_out/0", "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 6, 4]}; --tasks 2 printed task 1 = 1 prerequisite problem, factor counts [6, 5]. Assignment: root independent_ext_advance_payment takes 4, independent_ext_period_late_fee takes 6, independent_ext_annual_increase_fee takes 4. Occupied before this task: nothing (first task). Claimed here: the three policies above and tools assess_late_fee_72eb1d9b, record_annual_increase_315a2923, make_advance_payment_0a0cd4e1. Headroom left for task 1 (one prerequisite, factors 6 and 5): the move-out side of the charter - notice periods, fee end date and the final-month settlement of a residency that ends (fee end anchors, transfer to Larkspur care, surrender date) - is untouched, as are reservation cancellation and deposit refunds; task 1 claims the move-out side. Subject choice: service-fee and occupancy-change subjects are avoided because their base gates (pet_limits, second_occupant_allowed) are mixed-authority gates over a single correlation field that no single write can satisfy; credit subjects are avoided because every independent_credit write inherits the referral-credit gates.

[Design thesis] Surface goal: the POA daughter wants one payment that clears what is owed and prepays January (the December ACH autopay bounced on a closed account; parents away in January). Scored core: the advance amount (call 10, owner=user). Policy prerequisites between goal and core (both state form, value_input): (1) the advance waits on the ledger carrying a late fee entry for every period whose grace ended while past due -> the December 2026 late fee (agent, state_due, 6 factors); (2) the advance waits on the residency record showing the fee in effect for the first day of the coming month under an increase whose notice period has run -> the January 2027 annual increase (agent, state_due, 4 factors). Depth: goal -> prerequisite sentences -> two computations -> root computation. Breadth: ledger history (13 months, 81 rows), returned-payment reckoning, repeat-lateness count, residence length, payment standing, Entrance Fee Agreement plan (cross-difficulty, entrance), amenity quantities, oldest-charge-first application.

[Base-invariant card] late fee write (subject independent_late_fee_charge, governed by independent_late_fee): grace_period_elapsed - anchor the posting date of the period's monthly fee charge (2026-12-01, ledger row of the December base fee), duration payment_grace_days 10 calendar days, grace ends at end of 2026-12-11, exclusive -> assessable from 2026-12-12; frozen 2026-12-18 satisfies, 2026-12-11 would fail. one_late_fee_per_period - no late fee row with billing_period 2026-12 exists (only 2026-04). late_fee_on_live_residency - status active. Increase write (independent_rate_adjust, governed by independent_rate_adjustment): increase_notice_period - mailed 2026-10-09 + 60 days = 2026-12-08, inclusive; recording 2026-12-18 and effect 2027-01-01 both later; 2026-12-07 would fail. rate_guarantee_period - move-in 2019-05-13, guarantee ended 2020-05-13; increase_on_live_residency - active. At most one increase per 12 months: last increase effective 2026-01-01, next 2027-01-01. Payment write (independent_payment, governed by independent_payments_and_returns): payment_on_open_account - active; certified_funds_restriction - returned payments in 365 days = 1 (2026-12-05) < returned_payments_before_certified_funds 2, so a one-time ACH is accepted. Overrides declared: the increase policy supersedes base 'the fee recorded when the increase takes effect is the proposed fee from that notice' and the 7.5 percent ceiling sentence; the late fee policy supersedes the base past-due measure sentence and the greater-of sentence. The advance payment policy overrides nothing (base fixes no payment amount; it inherits oldest-charge-first application, pet_monthly_fee per pet without proration, storage and parking per billing month, second_person_fee while double).

[Business-object card] Residency ec9a7e11-... (W-214, One-Bedroom Deluxe, double with June Whitcombe). Late fee object: billing period 2026-12; rows included: 2026-12 base fee 3962.40, second person 1045.00, pet_monthly 40.00, storage_unit 45.00, covered_parking 55.00 (= 5147.40); payments in the month: ACH autopay 5147.40 of 2026-12-01; returns in the month: 5147.40 on 2026-12-05 referencing that autopay; excluded: the returned_payment fee (one-time, no billing period) and the April late fee. Increase object: the pending notice on the residency (rate_notice_date 2026-10-09, proposed 4279.39). Advance object: the residency account; the open balance is the whole ledger sum (charges in, payments and credits out). Every 2025-12..2026-11 statement is settled by its own payment; May 2026 autopay 5234.40 also settled the April late fee 87.00.

[Problem-tree card] root independent_ext_advance_payment (make_advance_payment_0a0cd4e1, owner user). Edge A: -> independent_ext_period_late_fee, kind value_input, gate open_balance, form state, sentence 'The advance amount is worked out only after the ledger carries a late fee entry for the billing period of the latest monthly fee charge whenever that period's grace period has ended with a past-due amount at or above the minimum that draws a late fee.' (affirmative), resolved by assess_late_fee_72eb1d9b (agent). False at opening: ledger has no 2026-12 late fee although the December charges (posted 2026-12-01) are unpaid after the 2026-12-05 return and grace ended 2026-12-11. Only the late fee policy's write books a late fee entry. Edge B: -> independent_ext_annual_increase_fee, kind value_input, gate coming_fee, form state, sentence 'The advance amount is not worked out until the residency record shows, as its fee in effect, the fee taking effect on the first day of the coming month under any annual increase whose notice period has already run.' (negated direction), resolved by record_annual_increase_315a2923 (agent). False at opening: monthly_service_fee 3962.40, rate_effective_date 2026-01-01, proposed 4279.39 pending, notice period ran 2026-12-08. Only the increase policy's write sets the fee in effect. Four-point test (both): ordering connective (only after / not until); a record-visible state (a late fee entry on the ledger; the fee in effect on the residency record); no tool, id or code token; scope exactly 'every billing period whose grace ended while past due' and 'any increase whose notice period has run'. Derivation: sentence + ledger (no December late fee, return posted) + late fee policy rule (it books the late fee) -> post the December late fee; sentence + residency (notice ran, fee unchanged) + increase policy rule (it records the fee taking effect) -> record the January increase. Topological order: late fee, increase, advance (the two prerequisites commute; replay both orders gives the same terminal state). Deletion sensitivity (Step 5 run): skipping the late fee -> advance 10518.01 instead of 10588.22; skipping the increase -> advance 10400.01. user_scenario names neither a late fee nor an increase; tools validate nothing.

[Factor card] Late fee (expected 70.21; baseline_result 0.00): past_due_reckoning method - tier 'payment returned within the month' (rows: autopay 2026-12-01 and its return 2026-12-05) -> 5147.40; baseline charges less payments 0.00 -> result 0.00. repeat_lateness parameter - one late fee in 12 months (2026-04-14, 87.00) -> 2.25 percent; baseline 1.5 -> 68.00. residence_length parameter - 91 months since 2019-05-13 -> 0.5 point; baseline 0 -> 95.95. entrance_plan_terms parameter, cross-difficulty entrance - occupied LifeChoice 75% Refundable Plan (fee_for_service) -> 0.25 point; baseline 0 -> 83.08. returned_fee_credit parameter, multi-source (returns in 12 months AND autopay in the month) -> 35.00; baseline 0 -> 105.21. daily_late_charge method - 7 days past the 2026-12-11 grace end, more than the 5 free days and fewer than 15 -> 7 x 4.00 = 28.00; baseline (no daily charge, the treatment for assessments within 5 days of the grace end) -> 42.21. Near-miss: the 2026-11-01 autopay is outside the one-month payment window and must not be netted; the April late fee lies outside the December period but inside the 12-month repeat count. Increase (expected 4150.61; baseline_result 4279.39): contract_ceiling parameter, multi-source (plan type AND the agreement names this residency), cross-difficulty entrance -> 6.0; baseline 7.5 -> 4210.05. residence_relief parameter - 91 months -> 1.0; baseline 0 -> 4190.24. standing_relief parameter - one return -> 0.25; baseline 0 -> 4160.52. fee_selection method - noticed 4279.39 > ceiling fee 4150.61 -> ceiling fee; baseline noticed fee -> 4279.39. Near-miss: the second person fee 1045.00 is billed but is not part of the increase. Advance (expected 10588.22; baseline_result 5195.61): open_balance_first method - open balance 5252.61 owed -> added; baseline statement alone 5335.61. registered_pets - latest pet charge quantity 1 -> 40.00 (baseline 10548.22); rented_storage - quantity 1 beyond the included unit -> 45.00 (baseline 10543.22); rented_parking - quantity 1 beyond the included space -> 55.00 (baseline 10533.22). Near-miss: the returned_payment fee 35.00 is in the open balance but is not a monthly amenity charge.

[Why a good test] A desk agent must notice two obligations the caller never mentions - the December late fee and the unrecorded January increase - by reading the advance policy's prerequisite sentences against the ledger and the residency record, then compute each with its own factors (returned-payment reckoning, repeat lateness, residence length, Life Plan terms, returned-fee credit, daily charge; contract ceiling, residence and standing reductions, ceiling selection), and only then hand Carol a single figure that also covers the open balance first and the January amenities. Difficulty is in reading and arithmetic, not tool choice: each tool is named by exactly one policy and blocks nothing.

[World rows] customers: Harold (identity: name, DOB 1939-07-22, ssn 1846; representative Carol, financial_poa, 9725550142). independent_residencies: one active residency (fee 3962.40 since 2026-01-01, notice 2026-10-09 proposing 4279.39, balance 5182.40). entrance_agreements: occupied LifeChoice 75% Refundable Plan naming the residency (decides contract ceiling and plan reduction; removing it moves the ceiling to 7.5 and the plan reduction to 0). independent_ledger: 13 months (2025-12..2026-12) of base, second person, pet, storage and parking charges with their payments (checks to April, ACH autopay from May), the April 2026 late fee 87.00 (drives repeat lateness), the December autopay, its return and the returned payment fee (drive the past-due reckoning, the returned-fee credit and the standing reduction). Removing the return would make the past-due amount 0 and no fee due; removing the April late fee drops the late fee percentage to 1.5. Automatic clauses checked: no other period is past due (every earlier statement paid), no waiver is requested, returned payments stay below the certified-funds count, no notice of termination exists, no credit balance is due back, no referral; no obligation outside this task is lit. Cache: account_balance 5182.40 equals the ledger sum (no deliberate cache trap; the advance policy reads the ledger).

[Persona] Carol speaks briskly in her own voice, volunteers only the bounced autopay, the trip and the wish to pay what is owed plus January in one payment she authorizes herself; identity details only on request; she agrees to anything the representative says must be posted first and runs the payment for exactly the amount given, then closes. She never names a late fee, an increase or a figure, and she never corrects the agent.

[Standard solution] find_customers(name, DOB) -> verify (DOB, ssn) -> read residency, ledger, entrance agreement -> unlock/call assess_late_fee_72eb1d9b(residency, 2026-12, 70.21) -> unlock/call record_annual_increase_315a2923(residency, 4150.61, 2027-01-01) -> unlock_user and hand over make_advance_payment_0a0cd4e1; Carol calls it with (residency, 10588.22).

[Verification run] .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py <diff> --task 0 -> '0.json 3 14 2 128 37 11 True ... COMPUTE OK' (handling-time recompute equals expected 70.21 / 4150.61 / 10588.22 and every factor_sensitivity and baseline_result). Order replay with the real tools: late-fee-then-increase and increase-then-late-fee give the same DB hash (True). check_extended, check_task_tools, replay_tasks, check_solvability, check_grounding, check_cross_fire all OK for --task 0.

[Revisions] (1) check_extended flagged a module-level helper as an unnamed task tool -> inlined the residency read in each tool -> EXTENDED OK. (2) replay_tasks flagged empty-string respite_stay_id as a dangling foreign key -> empty id fields seeded as null -> REPLAY OK. (3) First tool draft returned an Error when the residency was missing -> removed (a task tool checks no business condition).

[Draft recomputation from the visible context] Reading only the advance policy prose, the two prerequisite rules, the tool schemas and the rows the finders return: the advance waits on a December late fee entry (ledger shows none, return posted, grace over) and on the January fee in effect (record still 3962.40, notice ran 2026-12-08); the late fee rule gives 5147.40 past due, 1.50 percent -> 77.21, less 35.00, plus 7 x 4.00 -> 70.21; the increase rule gives ceiling 4.75 percent -> 4150.61 < 4279.39; the advance rule gives 5252.61 + 5335.61 = 10588.22. The same figures as gold; no second reading found.


[Round 2 rework - policy-task audit] F-1: the advance prerequisite sentence now reads 'The advance amount is worked out only after the ledger carries a late fee entry for the billing period of the latest monthly fee charge whenever that period's grace period has ended with a past-due amount at or above the minimum that draws a late fee.', scoped to the one period the late fee rule assesses and to the minimum that draws a fee, matching its condition. F-3: pet, storage and parking ladders charge the fee once for each unit at two or more (base 'per unit'). F-4: late fee tier 1 now reads 'where a returned payment was posted within the one month ending on the day of assessment', matching the compute. F-7: the daily late charge ladder now starts after daily_charge_free_days (5) days past the grace end: 15 or more days -> capped 60.00; 6-14 days -> 4.00 per day; 1-5 days -> none, a treatment reachable by assessments soon after the grace end. This world is unchanged by the rework (7 days -> 28.00; quantities 1): late fee 70.21, increase 4150.61, advance 10588.22, and every factor_sensitivity figure, re-verified by check_compute.

[Round 3 rework - policy-task audit revision 2] R2-O1: the past_due_reckoning tier label in factor_sensitivity now reads the reworded tier 'a returned payment was posted within the one month ending on the day of assessment'. No value of this task changed (70.21 / 4150.61 / 10588.22).
user_scenario: You are Carol Whitcombe-Ruiz, phoning the Larkspur Resident and Family Services desk on a Friday morning about your parents' independent living apartment, W-214 at Larkspur at Willow Creek in Plano, where your father Harold Whitcombe lives with your mother June. You hold your father's financial power of attorney and the desk has you on file as his representative. You are brisk, organized and a little embarrassed. Earlier this month your parents closed their old checking account when they moved their savings to a new bank, and nobody remembered that the monthly autopay still pointed at the old account, so the bank sent the December payment back. Your parents fly out tomorrow to spend the holidays and all of January with your sister in Scottsdale, and you want the apartment account squared away today: you want to pay whatever is owed right now and pay January's bill in advance, as one single payment, so that nothing can go late while they are away. You do not know what that figure should be and you expect the representative to work it out and tell you. You will authorize the payment yourself, as a one-time bank draft from your parents' new account, once the representative sets it up and hands it to you; you do not want anyone else to draw money, and you will enter the new account details yourself when you authorize it. Open by saying who you are and what you need in your own words. Only when the representative asks which account this is do you give your father's full name, Harold Whitcombe; only when asked to verify do you give his date of birth, 1939-07-22, and the last four digits of his Social Security number, 1846. If asked for a phone number, your father's is 9725550117 and yours is 9725550142; you do not remember his email address. If the representative tells you that something has to be put on the account or updated before the figure can be settled, you say that is fine and they should go ahead, since you only want the right number. When the representative gives you the amount and hands you the payment to authorize, you run it for exactly the amount you were given and read back the confirmation reference it shows. Once you hear the payment went through, you thank the representative and end the call.
